summary.headline: GPT Healthcare Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14.1% YoY to INR135.6 crore and PAT rose 45.2% to INR15.4 crore, but Raipur breakeven slipped to Q1 FY28.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR135.6 crore (up 14.1% YoY), with EBITDA up 23.9% to INR29.8 crore and EBITDA margin at 21.5%, up 150 bps. Network occupancy rose to 50.3% from 47.4%, driven mainly by an ~11% rise in inpatient volumes. Raipur, the newest hospital, remained loss-making at about INR9 crore in Q2 due to clinical attrition linked to new competition, including Artemis, and its breakeven was pushed from Q3 FY27 to Q1 FY28. Management reaffirmed FY27 revenue growth of 15-16% and the Jamshedpur 155-bed hospital launch in March/April 2027.

financial_highlights.value: ~INR9 crore in Q2; ~INR6.5 crore in H1

segments.name: ILS Salt Lake
segments.commentary: H1 occupancy 65.4% and highest network ARPOB at INR43,284; H1 revenue grew 12% YoY and the hospital crossed 850 robotic surgeries. Management later cited ~68% occupancy with limited room to grow.

segments.name: ILS Dum Dum
segments.commentary: Largest revenue contributor; H1 revenue INR84.8 crore, occupancy 69.4%, ARPOB INR43,086. Nephrology share cut to under ~15% from ~30%. Cardiothoracic and vascular surgery unit commenced; occupancy cited at ~74% later in the call.

segments.name: ILS Agartala
segments.commentary: H1 revenue growth 8.1% YoY, ARPOB INR40,254, occupancy about 55% (about 54% per an analyst's citation). Over 3,200 radiation therapy procedures on LINAC and over 1,000 PET scans in just over a year.

segments.name: ILS Howrah
segments.commentary: H1 revenue up 25% YoY, occupancy 45.8%. Orthopedics above 120 procedures a month; MAKO robotic knee system launched, nearing 100 robotic procedures.

segments.name: ILS Raipur
segments.commentary: First Central India hospital; Q2 revenue about INR9 crore, occupancy around 16.5%. NABH accredited within a year; 11 renal transplants; first TAVI and liver transplant in Q2. Breakeven guided at ~35% occupancy, now Q1 FY28 on a monthly basis.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of around 15% to 16% over FY26, with initial FY27 estimates reaffirmed.
Raipur breakeven on a monthly basis pushed to Q1 FY28 (earlier Q3 FY27); breakeven expected around 35% occupancy.
Average network occupancy expected at around 25% to 30% by end of Q4 FY27 (as stated; likely refers to the new Raipur/Jamshedpur ramp, not the network average).
FY28: Raipur expected to be marginally net positive; Jamshedpur expected to incur an EBITDA loss of about INR10 crore.
Raipur FY27 loss expected at about INR10 crore.
Jamshedpur 155-bed tertiary hospital to commence operations in March/April 2027; lease expense of about INR4 crore a year, similar to Raipur.
Targeting ROE and ROCE of about 25%.
Oncology revenue share at about 4% at Agartala-type hospital currently, expected to stabilise at 10% to 15% over the next four quarters.
capex_capacity: Jamshedpur 155-bed tertiary care hospital in Eastern India, on track to commence in March/April 2027; to be partly funded with debt.
Brownfield capacity of about 100 extra beds each at Agartala and Raipur, to be activated once occupancy is optimal.
No further brownfield bed addition possible at Kolkata hospitals (Salt Lake, Dum Dum, Howrah).
Management is evaluating greenfield and acquisition opportunities in Eastern India; no agreement signed. Ranchi MoU was not executed because the asset-light owner faced legal issues.
Cash of about INR45 crore in mutual funds and borrowings of about INR35 crore; management expects a mix of debt and equity for expansion.
demand_pricing: Network inpatient volumes rose ~11% YoY in Q2; Dum Dum and Howrah grew at double digits and Salt Lake around 10%.
Howrah focus on higher-end specialties; orthopedics above 120 procedures a month, with cardiology and nephrology being added.
Corporate patients (SAIL, Coal India and others) at Raipur are priced near CGHS rates, slightly above Ayushman Bharat rates; payment cycle within 90 days.
Management says its pricing is about 10% to 15% below peers Apollo, Fortis, Manipal and AMRI, with comparable service delivery.
International patient flow from Bangladesh is recovering slowly, with more visa requests but volumes still below historical levels.
Q2 ARPOB dip at Salt Lake, Agartala and Raipur was attributed to seasonal specialty mix; management called the network impact minor.

Supreme Court ruling on trade margins for essential medicines: management said the impact will be clearer after the order is issued in the November second week, and that service pricing will be adjusted to protect margins.
Competition: Artemis entered Raipur and drew away clinical talent, which caused the attrition.
Average length of stay: Salt Lake about 2.9 to 3 days; Dum Dum reduced from about 5.5 to 4.3 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ARPOB fall sequentially at Salt Lake, Agartala and Raipur, and what were the Raipur losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ARPOB drop is minor and seasonal, driven by fever-season specialty mix. Raipur losses were about INR9 crore in Q2 and INR6.5 crore in H1, in line with expectations.

qa_highlights.question: Has the Raipur breakeven timeline changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Breakeven was earlier guided for Q3 FY27 and is now expected in Q1 FY28 on a monthly basis, because of consultant attrition that has since been reversed. Tertiary hospitals typically take about 3 years to break even.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a bed-addition or expansion plan beyond Jamshedpur?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants to add hospitals every couple of years and is scouting greenfield and acquisition options in Eastern India, but will not sign deals just to expand. Agartala and Raipur can each add about 100 beds once occupancy is optimal.

qa_highlights.question: What are the lease costs for Raipur and Jamshedpur, and what are the FY28 losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Raipur lease is about INR4 crore a year, and Jamshedpur is expected to be similar. Raipur should be marginally net positive in FY28, while Jamshedpur is expected to have about INR10 crore EBITDA loss.

qa_highlights.question: What is the occupancy outlook for mature hospitals and key levers?
qa_highlights.answer: Salt Lake is at about 68% with limited room; Dum Dum at about 74%; Agartala at 55%, targeting about 70%. Howrah is growing via orthopedics, with cardiology and nephrology being added.

qa_highlights.question: How could the Supreme Court trade-margin cap affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is not yet clear and will be known after the order is issued in the second week of November. It said service pricing would be adjusted to maintain margins, since drug components are only part of overall service pricing.

risks_watch: Raipur remains below breakeven. Its Q1 FY28 target depends on retaining consultants amid competition from Artemis and new entrants.
Insurance empanelment at Raipur is about 70% complete; some insurers are still not on board.
Jamshedpur launch in March/April 2027 and its expected FY28 EBITDA loss of about INR10 crore.
Regulatory risk: proposed trade-margin cap on essential medicines (Supreme Court) and possible room-rent caps; management said the impact is still unclear.
Agartala occupancy at about 55% against a 70% target, which depends on adding consultants in a hard-to-staff location.
Bangladesh international patient recovery remains slow.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the core Kolkata network and FY27 growth guidance (15-16%), but more cautious on Raipur, where it conceded delayed breakeven. Answers on expansion and the Ranchi MoU were non-committal, and on the trade-margin ruling management said it was too early to quantify.
key_quotes: We are on track to achieving around 15% to 16% growth over last year.
We expect this hospital to break even by Q1 of next year on a monthly basis.
We do not intend to enter into an agreement just for the sake of expansion.
Operating at 80% occupancy is a very big challenge and very few hospitals are able to do it successfully.

adds.what: 155-bed tertiary care hospital in Eastern India (Jamshedpur)
Brownfield capacity of about 100 extra beds at Agartala
Brownfield capacity of about 100 extra beds at Raipur

growth.why: Management reaffirmed FY27 revenue growth of about 15-16% and Q2 revenue rose 14.1%, backed by ~11% inpatient volume growth and the Jamshedpur 155-bed hospital due March/April 2027, though Raipur breakeven slipped to Q1 FY28 and the brownfield bed additions are not yet scheduled.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 150 bps YoY to 21.5% in Q2 and 221 bps to 21.0% in H1, with occupancy up to 50.3% from 47.4%, though Raipur losses (~INR9 crore in Q2) and the Jamshedpur ramp (FY28 EBITDA loss ~INR10 crore) cap the upside.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Jamshedpur 155-bed tertiary hospital is under construction and on track to commence March/April 2027, to be partly debt-funded; brownfield 100-bed additions at Agartala and Raipur are planned but not yet scheduled.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Network inpatient volumes rose ~11% YoY in Q2 and management reaffirmed FY27 revenue growth of 15-16% (Q2 revenue +14.1%), though Kolkata hospitals are near capacity (Salt Lake ~68%, Dum Dum ~74%) and Raipur occupancy is only ~16.5%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 50.3% network-wide, so no urgent need, but Kolkata hospitals are near 68-74% occupancy with no further brownfield beds possible; management is scouting greenfield/acquisitions in Eastern India with no agreement signed and Ranchi MoU not executed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 revenue growth at 15-16% (H1 revenue +15.8%) but cut the Raipur breakeven timeline to Q1 FY28 and Raipur exit occupancy guidance is only 25-30% by Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raipur is ~INR9 crore loss-making per quarter with breakeven already slipped from Q3 FY27 to Q1 FY28 due to consultant attrition from Artemis entry; Agartala occupancy at ~55% vs 70% target and Supreme Court trade-margin cap is unquantified.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Howrah is adding cardiology and nephrology to orthopedics (120+ procedures/month), Dum Dum cardiothoracic/vascular unit has commenced, and oncology share at Agartala is targeted to rise from ~4% to 10-15% over four quarters; no dated launch beyond these.

rows.label: Supreme Court trade-margin cap on essential medicines
rows.why: Order expected in November second week; management says impact unclear and will adjust service pricing to protect margins, with pharmacy part of overall service pricing.

rows.label: Pricing 10-15% below peers
rows.why: Management says its pricing is 10-15% below Apollo, Fortis, Manipal and AMRI, which supports volume share but caps ARPOB growth (Q2 ARPOB +7.1% YoY to INR40,721).

rows.label: Raipur breakeven at Q1 FY28
rows.why: Q2 loss ~INR9 crore, H1 ~INR6.5 crore, occupancy ~16.5% vs ~35% breakeven; FY27 loss guided ~INR10 crore and consultant recovery is the key dependency.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Kolkata core network and reaffirmed 15-16% FY27 growth and the March/April 2027 Jamshedpur launch, but was cautious on Raipur's slipped breakeven and evasive on the Ranchi MoU, expansion beyond Jamshedpur and the trade-margin ruling; analysts probed Raipur losses, ARP

quality.why: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14.1% YoY to INR135.6 crore, driven mainly by ~11% growth in network inpatient volumes and occupancy up to 50.3% from 47.4%, with ARPOB up 7.1%; the brief lists no one-off items, acquisitions or excluded figures in this quarter's growth.
